threads.thread_goal: Align on membership tier structure, pricing, and policy constraints.

messages.text:
Kicking off the first draft of our tiered membership structure for the Launch of New Tiered Membership Sales Program project_title.

For T1, I have outlined 3 tiers in A1:
- Essential: entry option with basic benefits
- Plus: adds priority support and small discounts
- Premium: full bundle with highest discount and a couple of exclusive perks

Pricing bands are roughly aligned with what finance shared last quarter, but I have not yet had them re-confirm. I also started mapping policy constraints and eligibility rules in A5 so we can use that as the base for T2.

Can the sales team review the benefits and flag anything that feels hard to explain on calls or risky from a promise standpoint before I send this to legal and finance?

Thanks for sharing A1.

From a call flow point of view, 3 tiers feels manageable. A couple of questions so we can keep the pitch simple:
- For Essential vs Plus: is the main difference just support speed and a small discount, or are there any hidden conditions in A5 that we need to spell out?
- For Premium: the exclusive perks, are they limited in quantity or time-bound? That will matter for how we set expectations.

If we can keep each tier to 3–4 clear benefits, it will be easier to use later when we build the script for T3.

Looking at A1 and cross-checking with what I know about consumer rules, a few early flags before we go to legal and finance for T2:
- Any discount percentages should be clearly tied to a reference price and duration, otherwise it can be seen as misleading.
- For cancellations, A5 should state how refunds or partial periods work, especially for Premium.
- Upgrades and downgrades between tiers need clear timing rules so we do not overpromise on calls.

I suggest we avoid any wording like unlimited unless we are sure it is allowed under company policy.

I went through A1 and tried to imagine explaining this on a short inbound call.

Essential: feels straightforward if we position it as the starter option.
Plus: the mix of benefits is good, but I am not sure how to phrase the priority support without overcomplicating. Do we have a target response time we can safely mention in A5?
Premium: the exclusive perks might need concrete examples. Right now they sound attractive but a bit abstract.

Before we lock anything, could we maybe add one simple comparison line per tier in A1, like who it is best for? That would help later when we work on T3 and T7.

I also checked A1 and A5.

One thing I am not fully clear on: for Essential, are there any limits on how many times a member can use support or discounts per month? I did not see that spelled out, but maybe I missed it.

If there are limits, it would be good to add them into A5 so we do not say something on the phone that conflicts with T2 later when legal reviews.

Great questions.

On Essential vs Plus:
- Main difference is indeed support speed and a modest discount level.
- There are no hidden conditions planned, but I will add a short section in A5 clarifying response time ranges and any caps.

On Premium perks:
- They are time-bound, not quantity-limited. I will specify the duration and any blackout periods in A5.

I will also add a short 'best for' line per tier in A1 as suggested, to keep it easy to pitch later in T3.

Good call on the discount wording.

I will:
- Tie all discount percentages in A1 to a clear reference price and duration.
- Expand the cancellation and refund section in A5, especially for Premium.
- Add a simple rule for upgrade and downgrade timing so we can keep the message consistent.

Once I update A1 and A5, I will send them to legal and finance to complete T2, but I will wait for any other comments from the team first.

Once you add the 'best for' lines in A1, I think we can comfortably handle 3 tiers without confusing prospects.

From my side, I do not see a need to add a fourth tier. That would probably slow down calls and hurt conversion.

I would support going ahead with 3 tiers for launch, as long as A5 clearly lists the limits and timing rules you mentioned.

Agree on keeping it to 3 tiers for launch.

On pricing bands, the ranges in A1 look reasonable compared to what we see in the field. For launch, I would suggest:
- No stacking of membership discounts with other promos.
- A simple early-bird rule, for example a slightly better rate for the first month if they sign up in the first campaign wave.

We will still need finance and legal to validate this under T2, but if they are ok, I am comfortable using these bands in the script.

I am also in favor of 3 tiers.

From a conversation standpoint, I usually start with a quick question about how often they use our services. With the 'best for' lines in A1, it will be easier to match them to Essential, Plus, or Premium without going into a long explanation.

On pricing, I like the idea of a simple early-bird rule, but I want to be sure A5 spells out how long that rule applies so we do not accidentally extend it on calls.

I am ok with 3 tiers as well.

On the no stacking rule, I just want to confirm: if a customer asks about combining membership with a seasonal promo, should we always say it is not possible, or are there exceptions? Maybe we can add a short example in A5 so it is easier to remember during calls.

Thanks all, this is helpful.

Let us capture where we are:
- We go with 3 tiers: Essential, Plus, Premium.
- Each tier will have 3–4 clear benefits and a 'best for' line in A1.
- No stacking of membership discounts with other promos, unless finance and legal explicitly approve an exception.
- Early-bird rule: limited-time better rate for the first month of the campaign, details to be confirmed with finance.

I will update A1 and A5 accordingly and then send them to legal and finance to complete T2. Once they confirm, we can treat D1 and D2 as final for launch.
Once legal and finance sign off on T2, can you drop a short summary in the channel with any phrases we must avoid on calls? That will help us keep T3 and T7 aligned with A5 from day one.

Yes, I will add a short 'do not say' section in A5 after T2 is done and post a summary here.

That way, when we finalize the script and objection handling for T3 and T7, we can double-check that all wording matches the approved rules.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize sales script, objection handling, and pre-call checklist.

messages.text:
I have uploaded the first draft of the membership sales script and call outline in A2 for T3, plus a rough objection-handling cheat sheet in A3 for T7.

Structure in A2:
- Opening: quick context and permission to talk about membership
- Discovery: 3–4 questions to understand usage and budget
- Pitch: map them to Essential, Plus, or Premium based on A1
- Close: simple trial close and next steps

In A3, I listed 8 common objections from our past calls. I still need to add a couple more to reach 10.

Before we lock anything, can you all review and comment on tone, length, and any missing objections? Also, A7 is still empty; I plan to turn the key steps into a pre-call checklist once we agree on the flow.

I went through A2 and A3.

What works well:
- The discovery questions are short and open-ended.
- The mapping to tiers based on A1 is clear.

A few suggestions:
- In the opening, we might want a shorter version for busy prospects.
- For objections, we should add at least: 'I need to check internally' and 'We already have something similar'.

Also, we should double-check that none of the promises in A3 conflict with the policy notes in A5, especially around discounts and cancellations.

I like the structure in A2, especially the discovery part.

On tone, a couple of lines feel a bit too formal for our usual calls. For example, the way we introduce Premium might sound heavy if the customer is in a hurry.

In A3, could we also add an objection around language or understanding, like when someone says they are not sure they fully get the benefits? That comes up often when I talk to new customers.

I read A2 and A3 as well.

I am still getting used to the new tiers, so I might be missing something, but in the pitch section, I was not sure when exactly to propose Plus vs Premium. Maybe we can add one more example in A2, like a short scenario for each tier.

For objections, I agree we should include 'We already have something similar'. I hear that a lot when I call existing accounts.

Thanks for putting this together.

I checked A2 and A3 quickly against A5. Overall they look aligned, but we should tweak a couple of phrases:
- Anywhere we say 'unlimited', we should replace with the actual limits from A5.
- For cancellations, we should avoid promising immediate refunds and instead use the wording from A5.

Once we adjust those, I am comfortable validating T3 and T7 from a policy standpoint, but I will still send the final version to legal for a quick look.

Good points.

I will:
- Add a shorter opening variant in A2 for busy prospects.
- Include the two extra objections you mentioned in A3.
- Replace any 'unlimited' wording and align cancellation phrasing with A5.

I will also add a quick mapping example in A2 for Plus vs Premium, as suggested by others, so it is easier to decide on the fly.

On tone, I agree we should keep it closer to how we naturally speak.

I will go through A2 and simplify the Premium introduction, and I will add an objection in A3 for when the customer says they do not fully understand the benefits. The response can guide us to reframe the value in simpler terms or in their preferred language, in line with A5.

Once you make those edits, I think A2 will be in good shape for launch.

From my side, I would be ready to treat this as our standard script for the first wave, as long as we keep the door open to adjust after the pilot in T9 and T10.

Once the new version of A2 and A3 is up, I would like to do a couple of dry runs with someone before we start T9.

That will help me get comfortable with the shorter opening and the new objections, especially the ones about internal approval and existing solutions.

I am ok using A2 as the standard script too, once the edits are in.

For A3, could we list the objections in the order they usually appear in a call? That might make it easier to scan during a conversation.

I have updated A2 and A3 now:
- A2: added short opening, simplified Premium intro, and included mapping examples for each tier.
- A3: expanded to 10 objections, including internal approval, existing solutions, and lack of understanding. I also reordered them roughly by when they tend to show up in the call.

I used the exact limits and cancellation wording from A5 to stay compliant.

I reviewed the updated A2 and A3 against A5.

Everything looks aligned with the membership rules, and the promises are within what we defined in A1 and A5.

From my side, I am ok to validate T3 and T7 for launch, and I will still send them to legal for a quick final check. We can treat A2 as the standard script and A3 as the approved objection list for the first wave.

Great. To summarize for the team:
- A2 is our standard membership pitch script for launch.
- A3 contains the 10 approved objections and responses.
- Any new or unusual objections we hear during T9 should be logged so we can revisit A3 in T10.

I suggest we add a quick reminder in A7 to review A2 and A3 before each call.

I will now draft A7 based on the final A2 and A3.

Checklist items will include:
- Review A1 tier overview and 'best for' lines.
- Skim A2 script and choose opening variant.
- Keep A3 open for quick reference.

Once A7 is ready, I will share it here so we can all confirm it works in practice.

threads.thread_goal: Define target segments, outreach cadence, and prospect list priorities.

messages.text:
Starting the work on T4 and T5 for the Launch of New Tiered Membership Sales Program project_title.

For T4, I drafted 4 initial target segments based on our current base:
1) High-usage existing customers with no membership yet.
2) Medium-usage customers with irregular spend.
3) New customers in their first 90 days.
4) Dormant customers who have not purchased in 6–12 months.

I also created a first version of the prospect list in A4 with about 60 accounts tagged by segment.

For T5, I have a rough idea for cadence but would like your input before we finalize and document it in A6.

The 4 segments look solid to me.

From a conversion standpoint, I would prioritize:
1) High-usage existing customers.
2) New customers in their first 90 days.
3) Medium-usage with irregular spend.
4) Dormant customers.

In A4, we might want to add a simple 'priority' field so we can filter the list when we start T9.

I agree with the segments and the priority order suggested.

For dormant customers, I would just be careful not to spend too much time on them in the first 3 weeks. Maybe we can limit that segment to a smaller share of the outreach in A6.

I checked A4 and I like having the segment tags.

One question: for new customers in their first 90 days, do we have any rule in A5 about when we can start pitching membership? I want to be sure we are not contacting them too early.

Good point.

A5 does not forbid early outreach, but it suggests we wait until the customer has at least one completed order so we can tailor the pitch.

For the first 3 weeks, I would suggest we only include new customers who have at least one transaction in A4. I can add that note into A5 so it is clear.

Sounds good.

Let us lock the priority for the first 3 weeks as:
1) High-usage existing customers.
2) New customers with at least one transaction.
3) Medium-usage with irregular spend.
4) Dormant customers, with a smaller share of outreach.

I will update A4 with a 'priority' field and mark the accounts accordingly.

On T5, here is a proposal for outreach cadence to document in A6 for the first 3 weeks:
- Week 1: Day 1 call, Day 3 follow-up email, Day 6 call.
- Week 2: Day 10 email, Day 12 call.
- Week 3: Day 17 email, Day 19 final call.

Channel mix:
- High-usage and new customers: start with calls.
- Medium-usage and dormant: start with email, then call if they engage.

Open to tweaks before we treat this as final.

I like the structure.

One small suggestion: for high-usage customers, we might want one extra touch in Week 1, maybe a short message through digital channels between the first call and the email. That could be captured in A6 as an optional step.

For dormant customers, I would keep the cadence lighter to avoid feeling pushy. Maybe just one call and one email in the first 3 weeks, as a test.

We can still log them in A4 and track outcomes in A4 for T9 later.

I am ok with the cadence.

Could we add a simple field in A4 to track which touchpoint we are at? That would help when we prepare the weekly summary using A8 later.

Good call.

I will adjust A6 as follows:
- High-usage customers: add an optional digital touch between the first call and the first email.
- Dormant customers: limit to one email and one call in the first 3 weeks.

I will also add a 'touchpoint stage' field in A4 so we can track where each prospect is in the cadence.

From a membership operations point of view, this cadence looks manageable.

As long as we keep the touchpoint tracking in A4 up to date, it will also make it easier to review performance later.

I am comfortable approving this outreach cadence and channel mix for launch.

To recap:
- Priority segments for the first 3 weeks are set and tagged in A4.
- Outreach cadence and channel mix are defined in A6, with lighter touch for dormant customers and an optional extra touch for high-usage ones.
- A4 will track segment, priority, and touchpoint stage.

We can now start populating more accounts in A4 under T4 and then follow the cadence in T5.

threads.thread_goal: Run pilot, capture feedback, and refine tiers and messaging.

messages.text:
First batch of pilot membership calls for T9 is done.

Summary so far:
- 12 calls completed across segments 1–3 in A4.
- Using A2 and A3 as our guide.

Early observations:
- Essential and Plus are easy to explain; Premium takes longer.
- Most objections were about budget and needing internal approval.
- A few customers were confused about how discounts interact with other promos, even though we followed A5.

Logging detailed outcomes in A4 now. Sharing here so we can start thinking about T10 adjustments.

On my calls, I noticed that when I led with Plus instead of Essential, conversion was slightly better, especially for high-usage customers.

Premium only worked well when the customer already had a clear plan to increase their usage.

Also, a couple of people asked if they could try Plus for a month and then decide about Premium. I was careful not to promise anything beyond what A5 allows, but maybe we can clarify that path in A1 and A2.

I had 3 pilot calls.

Two customers liked the idea of Essential but wanted to know if they could upgrade later without losing the early-bird benefit. I was not fully sure how to answer, so I stuck to the wording in A5.

Maybe we can add a clearer line in A2 and A3 about how upgrades work during the campaign.

From my 4 calls:
- When I framed Plus as the default and Essential as the lighter option, people seemed more open to Plus.
- Premium felt like a stretch unless the customer already had a strong relationship with us.

On objections, budget and internal approval were indeed the main ones. A3 helped, but I felt we could use a slightly shorter response for the internal approval objection.

Thanks for the pilot insights.

From a membership perspective, it sounds like:
- Essential and Plus are landing well.
- Premium might need a sharper value statement or we keep it as a more selective offer.

On the upgrade and early-bird questions, A5 allows upgrades without penalty within the campaign window, but the early-bird rate does not extend automatically. I can make that clearer in A5 and A1.

Based on what we are seeing, I would suggest for T10:
- Keep all 3 tiers, but adjust the script in A2 so we usually lead with Plus for high-usage and new customers.
- Position Essential more clearly as a starter option, especially for budget-sensitive prospects.
- For Premium, tighten the pitch to focus on a couple of strong use cases instead of a long list of perks.

For A3, I can shorten the internal approval response and add a quick follow-up question to keep the conversation moving.

I like that direction.

If we keep Premium but make it more selective, maybe we can treat it as an 'if needed' option rather than something we always pitch. That would also reduce call time.

For the upgrade question, a simple line in A2 like 'you can start with Plus and review later during the campaign' would help, as long as it matches A5.

I agree with keeping all 3 tiers.

For me, the main challenge was explaining Premium quickly. If we can add one or two short examples in A2, that would make it easier to decide when to bring it up.

I am on board with the proposed changes.

One more idea: in A3, for the budget objection, we could add a short comparison that shows how the membership pays for itself after a certain number of uses, based on the pricing in A1. That might help close the gap for hesitant prospects.

Let us capture the main adjustments for T10:
- Keep 3 tiers as defined in A1.
- Update A2 so Plus is the default recommendation for high-usage and new customers, with Essential as the lighter option.
- Make Premium a more selective offer with clearer use cases.
- Clarify in A2 and A5 how upgrades work during the campaign and how the early-bird rule applies.
- Refine A3 responses for internal approval and budget, including a simple payback example.

If everyone agrees, we can proceed with these changes and treat them as our post-pilot refinement.

Works for me.

I will take the lead on updating A2 and A3 with the new positioning and examples, and I will sync with you on the exact upgrade and early-bird wording from A5 so we stay aligned.

I am aligned with these changes.

Once the updated A2 and A3 are ready, I would like to do a short role-play session so we can test the new Plus-first approach before the next pilot batch in T9.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on reporting format and weekly update ritual for membership performance.

messages.text:
I have set up the first version of the membership performance tracking sheet in A4 for T8 and a draft weekly summary template in A8 for T12.

A4 fields include: lead name, segment, tier pitched, tier sold, status, revenue, source, and touchpoint stage.

A8 has a simple structure for weekly updates: key numbers, highlights, lowlights, and next actions.

Please review and let me know if we are missing any fields or views that would help you report on T9 and the outreach cadence from A6.

A4 looks good.

I would add:
- A field for 'objection type' so we can see patterns from A3.
- A simple 'next step date' to keep follow-ups organized.

In A8, maybe we can include a small table that breaks down results by segment and tier, so we can quickly see where membership is working best.

Agree with the suggestions.

Also, could we add a field in A4 for 'script version' so we can distinguish between pre- and post-pilot versions of A2 and A3 when we look back at performance?

From a day-to-day perspective, A4 seems manageable.

For A8, I would appreciate a small section where we can add 2–3 qualitative notes from calls, not just numbers. That will help capture things that do not fit neatly into fields, like unusual objections or feedback on the tiers in A1.

I like the structure.

One question: how often do you expect us to update A4? After every call, or once a day? It would be good to agree on a simple rule so we stay consistent for T12.

Great inputs.

I will update A4 to include:
- Objection type.
- Next step date.
- Script version.

And I will adjust A8 to add:
- A small table by segment and tier.
- A short section for qualitative notes from calls.

On update cadence for A4, I suggest:
- Reps log outcomes and key fields the same day as the call.
- At minimum, everything should be up to date by end of day Friday so we can prepare the weekly summary in A8.

We can treat this as the standard for T8 and T12 unless there are objections.

That works for me.

For the weekly ritual, I propose:
- Each Friday by 16:00, we update A4.
- One of us posts the A8 summary in the channel, using the latest data.

We can rotate who posts the summary, but the format in A8 should stay the same so stakeholders can follow easily.

I like the Friday 16:00 rule.

Maybe we can also agree that any major insights from the week, like a new objection pattern or a big win, should be highlighted in the 'highlights' section of A8 so they do not get lost.

All good from my side.

Just to confirm: we will use A8 for the weekly summary, and A4 remains the single place where we log all call-level data for T9 and beyond.

The daily update rule is clear.

I might need a reminder at first, but once we get into the habit, it should be fine. Maybe we can add a small note in A7 to check A4 updates at the end of the day.

Let us formalize this.

- A4 is the central tracking sheet for all membership leads and outcomes.
- Reps update A4 the same day as calls, with everything current by Friday 16:00.
- A8 is the standard weekly summary template.
- Every Friday after 16:00, one of us posts the A8 summary in the channel.

With this, we have a clear reporting template and cadence for T8 and T12.

Agreed.

I can take the first weekly A8 summary this Friday so we test the flow and adjust if needed.
